SLICE 2 - COMPUTED vs NOT CHECKABLE, BY THE PRINTED CAPTION. A cell whose printed caption states a formula ENTIRELY in terms of other cells printed on this page is declared under _computed and is verifiable by recomputation from what the filled PDF prints. A cell whose printed caption sources its figure from an ATTACHMENT is writable input and is declared under _not_checkable with the caption as the reason, because nothing printed on the page could verify it. That one rule settles all of this page's total-shaped cells without a per-case decision. It follows the 433-F Section E footer precedent (433f.totals.json not_checkable.entries[0]) and its converse: rows the form has no slot for are dropped to an attachment and are NOT in a printed total, which is exactly what makes the other totals checkable, so a cell about precisely those dropped rows cannot be.

SLICE 2 - NO adapters/pdf/maps/433aoi.totals.json IS AUTHORED IN THIS SLICE, DELIBERATELY. run-form-gate.mjs step 10 checks a totals file whenever one EXISTS. Its feeder schema can add and it can subtract (a feeder may carry sign: -1); it cannot MULTIPLY and it cannot carry a printed CONSTANT. Two of this page's computed cells need exactly those: (3a) needs Times_7 = current market value X .8, and (1) needs 'Add lines (1a) through (1c) minus ($1,000)'. A totals file authored now would switch step 10 on while being structurally incapable of checking the two cells on this page that most need checking, and the other eight lines would report a clean pass beside them. That is the 'no declared state' condition this repo keeps finding defects in. So the arithmetic is declared here under _computed, verified by read-back in this slice, and step 10 stays SKIPPED with its reason printed until the feeder schema gains a factor and a constant. Recorded for Principal as a TOOL change, not a map change - the same direction of fix as generalising verify-form-coverage.mjs to accept a top-level _never_autofill.

SLICE 2 - NOTHING ON PAGE 2 IS DECLARED EXCLUSIVE, AND THAT IS A DECISION, NOT AN OMISSION. Page 1's option sets are exclusive because the page makes them so: a person is unmarried or married, and 'Do you' is one question with one answer. Page 2 prints THREE option lists - the bank account types on (1a) and (1b), 'Stocks / Bonds / Other' on (2a) and (2b), and '401K / IRA / Other' on (3a) - and prints no 'check one' instruction over any of them. One brokerage account can truthfully hold both stocks and bonds, so declaring that list exclusive would assert a constraint the page does not print and would hard-stop a truthful record. Little is lost: a group slot's checkboxes construct takes ONE input value and checks ONE box, so the read-back still shows exactly one box checked per row, and verify-form-coverage.mjs buckets the rest as 'checkboxes unchecked (independent)', which is an accounted-for state and not a gap. What IS lost is the guard against a box already set in the source PDF. Reported to Principal as arguable rather than resolved: the bank and the retirement lists are very likely exclusive in the world, and this map declines to say so because the page does not.

SLICE 2 - THE TWO BANK ROWS ARE NOT THE SAME SHAPE, AND THE MAP SAYS SO. Printed line (1a) offers SIX account types - Cash, Checking, Savings, Money Market Account/CD, Online Account, Stored Value Card. Printed line (1b) offers FIVE: the same list without Cash. So 1ab_bank_accounts declares six options on slot 0 and five on slot 1 rather than a uniform table, because check-row-shape.mjs reads declaredColumns PER SLOT and a uniform declaration here would be a claim about the page that is false. A record whose SECOND bank row says 'Cash' hard-stops on UNKNOWN CHECKBOX OPTION rather than filing silently under the wrong type or leaving the type blank.

SLICE 2 - equity MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS ON THIS PAGE, SO IT IS TWO COLUMN NAMES. On investments (2a)/(2b) and on life insurance (4a) the printed row is '$ [value] - $ [loan] = $ [line]', so equity = value minus loan, which is the backbone's investment.equity and life_insurance_policy.equity. On retirement (3a) the printed row is '$ [value] X .8 = $ [qsv] - $ [loan] = $ (3a)', so the same-shaped cell is QUICK SALE value minus loan. It is declared as quick_sale_equity, NOT equity, precisely so a future engine computing equity = value - loan uniformly cannot reach it. Giving them one name would make the 20% error a one-line mistake in a shared helper.

SLICE 2 - THE DIGITAL ASSET BLOCK IS BOUND AS SCALARS, NOT AS A GROUP, AND THE REASON IS THE ENGINE. Every other asset block on this page is a group, which buys row_class protection against a row landing in the wrong printed table. The digital asset block cannot be, because its row label carries a LONE checkbox ('Digital asset', box x 36.0..45.0 at y 378.9, printed word at x 50.4..94.0) with no counterpart cell, and fill-433aoi.mjs supports check_here only at the TOP LEVEL, not per group slot. Rather than invent a per-slot construct this slice cannot exercise, the block is bound as 2c_ scalars and its lone box under check_here. The form prints exactly one digital asset row, so nothing is lost today; when Section 9's digital asset questions are read, a per-slot check_here may be worth adding.

THE DEPENDENT TABLE HAS ONE FEWER ROW THAN 433-A's. 433-A's household_members group has five slots because that form prints Row4 twice (Row4[0] and Row4[1] carry the same leaf names). This form prints four rows and enumerates four; max is 4. check_here._why: A construct this form needs and 433-A does not. Every checkbox set on 433-A pairs an affirmative target with a negative one, so `checkboxes` can always name an option for either answer.
